narr: Thunderstorms developed across southeast Arizona in the afternoon, with strong cells pulsing up over terrain features and outflow boundaries. With precipitable water values near record levels for early-July and very slow steering flow, storms were capable of producing very heavy rain over the same areas, with rain rates around 1-2 inches per hour, resulting in localized flash flooding. Heavy rain from strong storms that developed over Pinal Peak experienced enhanced runoff due to the recent Telegraph burn scar. Runoff from these storms collected in the many dry washes with flow over forest service roads.
ev: A Tonto National Forest service member shared photos from a forest service road near Pinal Peak showing evidence of a flash flood with debris across the road, including boulders/rocks and tree branches strewn across the road. In coordination with the WFO Phoenix Senior Service Hydrologist, it would have taken at least 6 inches of flowing water to move the debris in the photos. There were no reports of damage or injuries.
